ravi (Finance): Heads-up: we're rolling out three billing/quota changes on May 15, 2026. TL;DR: new "Burst Credit Window", more itemized invoice line-items (by model & region), and a soft overage/auto-throttle policy. Full doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/2026-billing-update :megaphone:

emily (Sales): Are Dedicated customers affected?

ravi (Finance): Short answer: no disruptive changes for Dedicated reservations or enterprise contracts. Dedicated & Private customers keep contracted rates and quotas; itemized invoices will be available (easier chargeback). The new Burst Credit Window primarily affects hosted self-serve accounts.

jun (Eng): What exactly is the "Burst Credit Window"?

ravi (Finance): It's a short, predictable burst allowance that replaces the current transient burst behavior. Instead of opaque per-minute spikes, each account gets a small burst pool that refills over a rolling window. When it's exhausted we apply a soft throttle + queued retries for best-effort requests. This reduces surprise overage charges while keeping latency-sensitive paths available for paying tiers.

billing-bot: SAMPLE INVOICE: https://billing.redwood.internal/samples/itemized-invoice-2026.pdf (shows per-model, per-region line items and per-10k-token buckets) :page_facing_up:

kate (Customer Success): Free trials? we have customers who onboarded in last 30 days.

ravi (Finance): Free trial credit is being adjusted from 50k tokens to 30k tokens for new signups after May 15. Existing trialers created before that date will be grandfathered for 60 days to the old 50k amount. We'll send targeted emails and a console banner.

sasha (Prod Ops): Concern: new soft throttle could surface as 429s for some realtime flows. Any mitigation plan?

ravi (Finance): Good catch. We built a staged rollout: (1) opt-in beta starting Apr 20 for high-volume customers, (2) global rollout May 15 with a 14-day elevated-grace period where requests are queued rather than charged/blocked, (3) after grace, soft throttles + queue fallback kicks in. For critical customers we can whitelist or increase burst pools manually during migration. If you see regressions open a ticket in #eng-oncall with "billing-throttle" tag.

emily (Sales): How will refunds / credits work if we accidentally throttle a customer during migration?

ravi (Finance): We'll auto-apply credits for customers who experience sustained throttling caused by the rollout (>= 1 hour of degraded service) and CS will have a fast-track dispute flow. We'll also publish a reconciliation sheet for finance & partner teams.

jun (Eng): Any impact to SDK rate limiters or client libraries?

ravi (Finance): Minimal. SDKs will get a minor release with a 429->retry guidance and builtin jitter recommended config. We strongly encourage teams to adopt exponential backoff + idempotency tokens for writes.

kate (Customer Success): Ops question — will invoices show charges per model and zone? that's what customers keep asking for.

billing-bot: Yes — new invoices include: model name, region, token buckets (prompt/completion), effective unit price, and a "burst usage" line item. Example: model/redwood-v1 | us-west-2 | 120k prompt tokens | $X.XX

sasha (Prod Ops): If a customer wants to opt out and keep current behavior, is that possible?

ravi (Finance): For enterprise & Dedicated customers, yes (keep current behavior by config). For hosted self-serve, opt-out is available during the 60-day window for existing accounts—after that the new behavior becomes standard. If a customer needs longer, CS can request an extension via finance@redwood.com.

emily (Sales): Any changes to pricing tiers?

ravi (Finance): No headline price changes today. We are introducing a new "burst add-on" SKU for customers who want larger immediate burst capacity without changing reserved throughput. That's optional.

kate (Customer Success): Action items for CS: scheduled emails to affected customers (auto), updated help center article, migration checklist, and a CSV of impacted accounts. I'll coordinate with Ops & Growth.

sasha (Prod Ops): I'll add a dashboard for burst pool exhaustion and per-customer throttle events.

ravi (Finance): Thanks. If you need adversarial test cases, we have a staging policy: set header X-Redwood-Billing-Test: true to simulate burst exhaustion. Questions -> #billing-questions or finance@redwood.com. Exec signoff: Ravinder (CFO). :white_check_mark:
